lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and a `@app.get("/")` route returning {"Hello": "World"}. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in the browser.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the GET route for the root path
Server is up; open this URL in the browser
The JSON object returned by the root route

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server used to run FastAPI apps
The @app.get decorator defines a path for the HTTP GET method
The "/" path is the root route; visiting it calls the function
uvicorn main:app means file name, then app variable
--reload restarts the server automatically when the file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn. Then create main.py in a new project folder.
In main.py, import FastAPI, create app = FastAPI(), and decorate a function with @app.get("/") that returns a dict like {"Hello": "World"}.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder that contains main.py. 'main' is the file name without .py and 'app' is the variable name.
Once the terminal shows 'Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000', open that URL in your browser to see the JSON.
common_mistakes: Installing only fastapi and not uvicorn, which gives 'command not found: uvicorn'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, which raises 'Could not import module "main"'.
Typing uvicorn main.py:app instead of uvicorn main:app.
Naming the instance something other than app (e.g. api = FastAPI()) but still running main:app, which gives 'Attribute "app" not found'.
Forgetting the parentheses in FastAPI() or the leading @ on the decorator.
Naming the file fastapi.py, which shadows the library and breaks the import.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add an empty `items = []` list and a `@app.post("/items")` function `create_item(item: str)` that appends the item and returns the list. Test it with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Empty in-memory list that holds the items
POST endpoint at /items
curl response: the current items list

explanations.topic: An HTTP POST to /items calls create_item
A plain str argument is read as a query parameter
Return the whole list so you can see each added item
Passing the item with ?item= in the URL

hints: Define an empty list named items at module level, above the route functions.
Decorate the new function with @app.post("/items") so it handles POST requests, not GET.
Inside create_item(item: str), call items.append(item) and then return items.
Keep uvicorn running and send the request from a second terminal: curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'.
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Defining items = [] inside the function, which resets the list on every request.
Leaving the URL unquoted in the shell, so ? or & get interpreted by the shell.
Forgetting the ?item=... query string, which gives a 422 'field required' error.
Sending curl in the same terminal as uvicorn, or not restarting/reloading the server after editing.

steps.title: Add GET item by ID endpoint
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with `get_item(item_id: int)` returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items with POST, then run `curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0`.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with item_id path parameter
Fetch the first item by index

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly brackets map URL segments to function arguments
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Path value becomes the function's parameter
Type hints let FastAPI convert the path string to int
Requesting a missing index gives an internal server error

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator as before, but put the variable part of the path in curly brackets: /items/{item_id}.
The function parameter name must match the name inside the curly brackets, and give it the type hint int.
Return items[item_id]. Saving reloads the server and empties the list, so POST a couple of items again before testing.
Test with: curl -X GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0 and you should get back the first item you added.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-adding items. The reload resets items to [], so index 0 gives an internal server error.
Parameter name in the function doesn't match the {item_id} in the path, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Leaving out the int type hint, so item_id is a string and indexing the list fails.
Using a hyphen instead of underscore, or a different path such as /item/{item_id}, so the curl URL doesn't match.
Expecting a 404 for a missing index. At this step it is a 500 Internal Server Error, which the next step fixes.

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import `HTTPException` from fastapi and in get_item raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")` when the index is out of range. Re-run curl for a missing item, e.g. /items/47.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi
Raise a 404 when the item is missing
curl now returns a helpful 404 detail

explanations.topic: HTTP status codes: missing item is a client error
404 Not Found is the right response
detail parameter adds error context

hints: Look at the top of main.py: is HTTPException imported alongside FastAPI?
In get_item, check whether item_id is less than len(items) before indexing.
If the item doesn't exist, raise (not return) HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...).
Save the file so uvicorn --reload picks it up, then re-run the curl request for an ID that doesn't exist.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`, which sends a 200 response.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError (shown as a 500 error).
Using `<=` instead of `<` in the bounds check, so the last index still raises an IndexError.
Writing the detail as a plain string instead of an f-string, so the literal text {item_id} appears.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not using --reload), so the old 500 error persists.

steps.title: Add list endpoint with limit
steps.instructions: In main.py add `@app.get("/items")` with `list_items(limit: int = 10)` returning `items[0:limit]`. Test with `curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.

targets.caption: New list endpoint taking an integer limit query parameter
Request only the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Query parameters: function args not in the path become query params
FastAPI converts query strings to the annotated type (int)
Same path, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value in the function header applies when limit is omitted

hints: Use the same '/items' path as the POST endpoint, but decorate it with @app.get instead.
Add a parameter like limit: int = 10 to the function. Since it's not in the path, FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return a slice of your list: items[0:limit].
POST a few items first, then test with curl -X GET 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the type hint `int`, so limit stays a string and slicing fails with a TypeError.
Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the request hits the create_items endpoint.
Not quoting the URL in curl, so the shell interprets '?' or '&'.
Testing after restarting the server without adding items again, which returns an empty list [] because the list is in memory.
Running uvicorn without --reload and not restarting it after adding the new route, which gives 405 Method Not Allowed.

steps.title: Model items with Pydantic BaseModel
steps.instructions: Import `BaseModel` from pydantic, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and use `item: Item` in create_item and `-> Item` in get_item. POST JSON with curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}'.

targets.caption: The Pydantic model for an item
Boolean field with a default of False
Response is an object matching the model

explanations.topic: Why use Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, code completion
Model arguments are read from the JSON payload, not query parameters
Default values: is_done defaults to false
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Start by adding `from pydantic import BaseModel` at the top of main.py.
Create `class Item(BaseModel):` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, then change create_item's parameter to `item: Item`.
Annotate get_item with `-> Item` so it returns the model.
The old `?item=apple` query URL no longer works. Send JSON: curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter (?item=apple), which gives a 422 because the body is missing.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in the curl request.
Defining Item without subclassing BaseModel, so FastAPI does not parse it from the body.
Using single quotes inside the JSON payload. JSON keys and strings need double quotes.
Removing the default on text, then sending a payload without text and being surprised by the validation error.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=Item` to the get-item decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list-items decorator. Let uvicorn reload and confirm responses still return item objects.

targets.caption: Declare the response model on the get-item route
Response model for the list endpoint

explanations.topic: Reusing the Pydantic BaseModel to describe responses
response_model argument in the route decorator
Response model as a contract for clients and front-ends

hints: Response models go in the route decorator, not the function body: add a response_model argument to @app.get.
For the single-item route use response_model=Item; for the list route wrap it: response_model=list[Item].
If list[Item] errors on older Python (<3.9), import List from typing and use List[Item].
Save and let uvicorn --reload restart, then request /items and /items/0 to confirm item objects still come back.
common_mistakes: Putting response_model on the function signature instead of inside @app.get(...).
Using response_model=Item on the list endpoint, which fails validation because a list is returned.
Using list[Item] on Python 3.8 or older, causing a TypeError at startup.
Typo like response_models or responseModel, which FastAPI rejects as an unexpected keyword.
Returning plain strings or dicts missing required Item fields, now causing a ResponseValidationError (500).

steps.title: Explore interactive API documentation
steps.instructions: With `uvicorn main:app --reload` running, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, use Try it out on POST /items and Execute. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click 'Try it out' on POST /items, edit the request body, then click Execute
Sends the request and shows the curl command plus the response body
Link under the title that opens the raw OpenAPI JSON schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods and parameters
Try it out / Execute sends a real request and shows the curl command
/redoc is an alternative documentation view
/openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in the browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint, click 'Try it out', edit the JSON request body to match your Item model, then click 'Execute'.
Scroll down below Execute to see the curl command and the Response body; the terminal should log a 200 for POST /items.
Change the path to /redoc for the alternative docs, and click the small /openapi.json link under the title for the raw schema.
common_mistakes: Opening /docs while the uvicorn server is stopped, so the page fails to load
Forgetting to click 'Try it out' first, so the request body isn't editable
Sending a request body that doesn't match the Pydantic Item model, resulting in a 422 validation error
Leaving the body as the example with wrong types (e.g. a string where a bool is expected)
Typing the URL with a trailing typo like /doc instead of /docs
